title: Test the GetExtendedTcpTable decoding (address and port byte order, IPv6 rows) against a real loopback connection
outcome: engram_tcp_connections and engram_tcp_table in src/engram_host_identity.rs decode the Windows owner-pid TCP tables (dwRemoteAddr.to_ne_bytes, u16::from_be(raw as u16), IPv6 rows, the row offset after the count), and no test reads a real table. A byte-order regression on the remote address could turn an SSH connection to this machine's own address into a foreign one and give credit that should be withheld; a port-order regression would break the -L forward exclusion. A #[cfg(windows)] test opens a TcpListener on 127.0.0.1 and an IPv6 [::1] one, connects a TcpStream to each, and asserts that engram_tcp_connections() lists rows with pid == std::process::id() and the exact local and peer SocketAddrs (127.0.0.1 reversed would read 1.0.0.127).
acceptance: A Windows-only test asserts that engram_tcp_connections() reports this test process's own established IPv4 and IPv6 loopback connections with their exact local and peer addresses and ports.
